 Boyce woman convicted in nearly $10 million federal tax refund fraud scheme
 November 20, 2026 November 20, 2026 / JSLLC 
 File Photo 
 BOYCE, La. — A 64-year-old Boyce woman was convicted Tuesday, Nov. 17, on federal fraud, obstruction and money laundering charges stemming from a scheme involving nearly $10 million in fraudulent tax refund claims.
 Jane Frances Pierce was found guilty by a federal jury of mail fraud, filing false tax returns, corruptly interfering with an Internal Revenue Service investigation and money laundering, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana.
 Federal prosecutors said Pierce filed false tax returns through a purported trust she controlled, claiming nearly $10 million in refunds. She received more than $1 million from the IRS and used the money for personal expenses, including purchasing a home and paying mortgages for relatives.
 When the IRS attempted to recover the money, Pierce tried to obstruct the investigation by filing a false amended tax return, mailing a fraudulent check to the agency, submitting a false court document and laundering the remaining proceeds, prosecutors said.
 Pierce also filed a separate false tax return on behalf of a purported estate she controlled, seeking more than $7 million in additional refunds.
 The jury deliberated approximately 40 minutes before returning guilty verdicts on all counts.
 Following the verdict, the court ordered Pierce held in custody pending sentencing, scheduled for Feb. 16, 2027.
 Pierce faces maximum penalties of 20 years in federal prison for mail fraud, 10 years for each money laundering charge and three years for the false tax return and corrupt interference charges. She also faces possible restitution, supervised release and financial penalties.
 The actual sentence will be determined by a federal judge after consideration of federal sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors.
 IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas Johnson and Justice Department Trial Attorney Hayter L. Whitman prosecuted the case.
